raw_response.printed_headline_estimate: GEE models of log-transformed operator volumetric revenue ($/m3) (Table 5, PDF p. 13 / printed p. 12; >3,900 monthly records from 5 operators in Ghana, Rwanda, and Uganda; Archetype 1 Multi-country N = 1,680 off-premises + 2,094 on-premises revenue-month records): Tariff level beta = 0.470 (SE = 0.0319, 95% CI [0.407, 0.532], P < 0.001); On premises connections interaction beta = -0.034 (SE = 0.0429, 95% CI [-0.118, 0.050], P = 0.429); Prepaid credit interaction beta = -0.075 (SE = 0.0691, 95% CI [-0.210, 0.061], P = 0.279); Archetype 4 Public Prepaid credit interaction beta = -0.166 (SE = 0.0418, 95% CI [-0.248, -0.084], P < 0.001). Also one-way ANOVA/t-tests on log volumetric revenue across service areas and operators (Table 2, PDF p. 9, P < 0.001) and one-way ANOVA on population density (PDF p. 8, p > 0.05). Water volume dispensed (m3/wp/mo, Tables 3-4) is reported descriptively only.
raw_response.publication_year_note: Published 28 June 2022 in Environ. Res.: Infrastruct. Sustain. Volume 2 (2022), article 035003 (received 8 December 2021, revised 14 March 2022, accepted 29 March 2022).
raw_response.rationale: The study conducts inferential quantitative analyses—generalised estimating equation (GEE) regressions (Table 5, PDF p. 13) and one-way ANOVA / Student's t-tests (Table 2, PDF p. 9)—testing how tariff levels, connection type (on- vs. off-premises), and payment modality (prepaid credit vs. pay-as-you-fetch / monthly billing) relate to log-transformed volumetric operator revenue ($/m3). However, all inferential models fail Criterion 4 because the tested outcome is an operator financial revenue-collection metric (revenue collected per cubic metre dispensed, explicitly normalised to remove differences in user counts and consumption rates) rather than a household or community water service access outcome (connection, coverage, availability, reliability, continuity, per-capita quantity, affordability, or exclusion). Aggregate water volume dispensed per waterpoint (Tables 3-4) is reported only with descriptive statistics without inferential tests, and the authors note that lack of user population data prevents analysing service area penetration, per-capita water usage, actual end-user prices paid, or service reliability.
